title: A rule
description: A rule (rules/R<number>.yaml). The identifier is the file name without its ending. The value lists of languages and repositories are empty for now: items is false until the pull request that brings the first item needing a value adds it as an enum.

statement.description: The rule as one plain sentence on one line. Reasons and examples never stand in it.

languages.description: Absent means every language. Within the field one value must fit.

repositories.description: A node of the tree: foreign and own below everywhere, public and internal below own, customer below internal. The rule holds from the node it names downwards. Absent means everywhere a member of the organization works, someone else's project included. Within the field one value must fit; between the fields all must fit.

applies-when.description: A condition under which the rule applies.

enforced-by.description: review, or the names of the automated checks as their owner calls them (lowercase words, hyphens, slashes).

principles.description: The principles the rule follows from.

next.description: Announcement of a stricter step: what is to hold from a named version on. It does not take effect by itself: a pull request takes the step by raising level or existing and removing next.

from.description: A version that can carry an incompatible change: X.0.0, or 0.Y.0 below 1.0.0.

rationale.description: The failure the rule prevents or the property it secures, as Markdown text without headings.

examples.description: Examples of meeting and violating the rule, as Markdown text without headings; code blocks included.

replaced-by.description: The rule that took the place of a retired rule.

allOf.description: A rule addressed to the repository or the organization cannot hold in someone else's project, so it names own or a node below it.

level.description: required: a deviation needs the deviation process. recommended: a deviation needs a reason. permitted: states that something is allowed.

existing.description: What holds for what was there before the rule. exempt: nothing. on-touch: brought in line when touched anyway. required: brought in line.
